text:
mike: Heads-up — since yesterday's OFED/kernel roll in eu-central we've seen a ~3-5x jump in allreduce tail latency for larger jobs. NCCL logs show repeated transport fallbacks (IB -> TCP) and some jobs are queueing behind the slower paths. :rotating_light:
anya: Do we have a scope? all clusters in eu-central or a subset of racks? any pattern by instance type?
mike: Looks concentrated to the gfx-pool (A100s) in eu-central-1a/b. ~18% of multi-node jobs touched the fallback. Single-node unaffected. No config changes to apps.
jamie: Which OFED/kernel/drivers were rolled?
mike: Rolling summary: OFED 5.8.1 -> 5.9.0, kernel 6.1.45 -> 6.4.9, nvidia driver 535.86 -> 536.10. Mellanox firmwares unchanged for now.
lee: Any link errors in dmesg or rdma logs?
mike: Yep — seeing a lot of "Link training timeout" and some rdma_cm -110 connection errors around the time of job startup. Example snippet:
```
[  123.456789] mlx5_core 0000:03:00.0: link training timeout on port 1
[  123.456801] rdma: rdma_create_qp failed: -110
[  123.456812] rdma_cm: conn_req from 10.0.12.7 failed: -110
[  123.456823] containerd: task: failed to start: exit status 1
```
anya: Hmm. That matches link training failing then NCCL falling back after timeout negotiation. Do we have counters (port counters/slow link events) from the switches?
mike: Switch counters look clean, no physical error spikes, which suggests training is failing at the NIC/firmware/driver handshake rather than the fabric.
jamie: Two broad mitigations: 1) roll back OFED/driver to previous known-good for the affected pools; 2) force a temporary software fallback to TCP for affected jobs to avoid intermittent IB negotiation which causes retries and backpressure.
lee: For short term we can set NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 on the job launcher to force TCP. That will increase inter-node CPU/network cost but keeps jobs moving instead of flapping between transports. Set via our k8s job env or ray/native launch templates.
sarah: Cost hit? If we go TCP for 18% of jobs, rough CPU/network uplift?
mike: Early estimate: cross-node bandwidth efficiency drops ~2x for some allreduce patterns; estimated incremental cost 15-30% on those jobs. Better than repeated retries and long tails though.
infra-bot: deploy-bot triggered: "Canary env update: set NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 for gfx-pool jobs in eu-central a/b" by jamie — scheduled now. :white_check_mark:
anya: Good. Meanwhile can we collect NIC logs and enable mlx5 debug counters across a small canary to capture link training handshake? Need mlx5 logs + rdma debug level and full mlx5 fw dump.
mike: On it. Spinning up a 4-node canary and enabling detailed logs. I also captured tcpdump of the negotiation window and nv_peer_mem traces.
jamie: Ops plan for rollback if canary shows consistent success: 1) pause OFED roll for remaining racks, 2) roll back the drivers on affected nodes to previous package, 3) re-run a small perf suite (allreduce/bert/hf) to validate.
lee: Can we instead patch mlx5 parameters to increase training timeout thresholds as a lower-risk experiment? Might be a kernel/module param we can tweak temporarily. If that makes the handshake succeed we avoid full rollback.
mike: There's a module param in some kernels but it's not universally available across our fleet. I'll test on canary. If it helps, we can push a sysctl/module-arg job via ansible.
sarah: Timeline — engineering is blocked on some E2E CI that runs multi-node. Do we have an ETA to revert or mitigate?
jamie: If canary logs look good within 90 minutes, plan to rollback OFED only on the 6 most impacted racks in the pool within the next 3 hours (rolling), otherwise keep forcing TCP for the jobs and schedule full rollback overnight.
anya: Also flagging customers who may be affected — cc @customer-ops for visibility and to prepare messaging if rollback affects scheduled windows.
mike: Notes for postmortem: correlate job start time with link training failures, capture firmware/driver versions, and include whether forcing TCP reduced tail latency. Also include cost delta for affected jobs.
lee: On the technical side, we should add a transport-health check in the node agent that runs a small RDMA handshake preflight and marks node as 'rdma-healthy' only if handshake succeeds. That would prevent scheduling multi-node GPU jobs on flaky nodes.
jamie: +1 — that would avoid job-level retries and surface hardware issues earlier.
infra-bot: alert: monitoring created: "eu-central gfx-pool rdma link_training_timeouts" — paging rule set to 15-min aggregation.
mike: Will post canary logs here once captured. Thanks all. :eyes:
